title: Momentum and Impulse
seo_title: SSS 2 Physics: Momentum and Impulse Worksheets (WAEC/NECO)
standard_text: Momentum, p = mv, as a vector; Newton's second law in terms of momentum, Fnet = Δp/Δt; the conservation of linear momentum in an isolated system; elastic and inelastic collisions; impulse, FnetΔt = Δp, and safety devices. (summary of the senior secondary Physics curriculum, SSS 2; WAEC and NECO syllabuses)
meta_desc: Free SSS 2 Physics worksheets (senior secondary curriculum, WAEC and NECO): momentum and impulse, momentum and impulse problems, collisions, momentum problems and impulse and safety. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: In an isolated system the total momentum is conserved.
body_html:
How to think about it

Momentum is the product of mass and velocity, p = mv; it is a vector, so choose a positive direction. Newton's second law can be written as Fnet = Δp/Δt: the resultant force equals the rate of change of momentum.

In an isolated system (no external resultant force) the total momentum before a collision equals the total momentum after it. In an elastic collision kinetic energy is also conserved; in an inelastic collision it is not. Impulse FnetΔt = Δp: airbags, crumple zones and arrestor beds increase Δt, which reduces the force.

Example

A 2 kg ball at 3 m·s⁻¹. Momentum?

p = mv

Answer: 6 kg·m·s⁻¹

Example

A 1 kg trolley at 4 m·s⁻¹ joins a 1 kg trolley at rest. Common velocity?

Total p = 4

Answer: 2 m·s⁻¹

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting that momentum has a direction.
  • Thinking kinetic energy is conserved in every collision.
  • Thinking an airbag reduces the change in momentum.

faq.q: How does an airbag reduce injury?
faq.a: It increases the time over which the momentum changes, so the force on the passenger is smaller.
When no external resultant force acts on the system (an isolated system).

items.q: An 8 kg gun fires a 0.0250 kg bullet at 450 m/s. What is the recoil speed of the gun?
items.e: Momentum is conserved: MV = mv, V = 0.0250 × 450 ÷ 8 = 1.41 m/s.

items.q: Usman finds that a helmet's foam makes a stop take 0.06 s instead of 0.02 s. The change in momentum is the same. How does the force compare?
items.e: F = Δp ÷ Δt: 3 times the time → 1/3 of the force.
